podcast.body: This album is referenced as a significant later work, from which the live version of "Whistleblower" was taken. "Arkels in a live version of Whistleblower, a track from their 2011 album Michigan Left."

podcast.body: This album took three years to release after "Jackson Square," recorded at The Bathhouse studio in Bath, Ontario, which is owned by The Tragically Hip. Initial demos were made at the Tokyo Police Club space and in Dan's basement. It was the band's first time self-producing a record with Dan, leading to a somewhat unfocused but experimental month-long process where they tried new arrangements, instrumentation, and effects like delays and gated reverb, and became more open to synth sounds ("Hollow notes"). The album was completed before they signed with Universal, so it was not conceived as a major label record. "This was also your first major label album."
